paper.title: Better Algorithms for Stochastic Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions

unmapped: Adaptive adversary: corruptions on round t may depend on past player choices and current/past stochastic rewards
C = sum_t ||tilde R^t - R^t||_inf is a realized random variable, unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote: A stochastic reward $\rew^t_i \in [0,1]$ is drawn for each arm $i$ from its reward distribution; The adversary observes the vector $\rew^t$ and generates corrupted rewards $\wt{\rew}^t \in [0,1]^K$; The player picks $i_t \in [K]$, possibly at random, and observes the corrupted reward $\wt{\rew}^t_{i_t}$. ... $C = \sum_{t=1}^T \norm{\wt{\rew}^t - \rew^t}_\infty$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with Adversarial Corruptions (lower bound)
unmapped: Lower-bound instance uses deterministic rewards 0 and 1 with an adversary randomly swapping them
settings.definition_quote: Consider the case of two arms with deterministic rewards $0$ and $1$, and consider an adversary that at each time step swaps the rewards of the arms with probability $1/2$.

algorithms.name: BARBAR (Bandit Algorithm with Robustness: Bad Arms get Recourse)

conditions: C is the realized corruption level (random variable)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of \cref{alg:barbar} is bounded by \[ O\Bigg(KC + \sum_{i \neq i^\star} \frac{\log{T}}{\Delta_i} \log\!\Big(\frac{K}{\delta}\log{T}\Big) \!\Bigg). \]

results.notes: Regret is pseudo-regret sum_t (mu* - mu_{i_t}), bounded with probability 1-delta. Agnostic to C. Appendix B shows Omega(KC) is tight for this algorithm.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: To convert the bound of \cref{thm:main} into a bound on the expected regret of the algorithm, one can set $\delta = 1 / T$; ... Thus, the expected regret is bounded by O(K\,\Ex[C] + \sum_{i \neq i^\star} \frac{1}{\Delta_i} \log^2(KT)).

results.notes: Derived informally in text after Theorem 1, not a separately numbered statement.

source.quote: We show an $\Omega(C)$ lower bound for the pseudo-regret of any algorithm. ... In other words, for the pseudo-regret under this contamination model there is a lower bound of $\Omega(C)$ that holds for all $C$ up to $T \div 2$. Moreover this lower bound holds even for the case of known $C$.

results.notes: Informal argument in discussion; says 'with constant probability the algorithm will suffer pseudo-regret Omega(C)', so the probability type is loosely stated.
